quizName: DMV Practice Test #6 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: What should be your first priority when buying a motorcycle helmet?
questions.correctAnswerText: Protection
questions.explanation: Protection should be your first priority. Choose a helmet that fits snugly, fastens securely, and has a DOT approval sticker.

questions.question: If you need to stop quickly, you should:

options.text: Use both the front and rear brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the front and rear brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: To stop quickly, press both the front and rear brakes at the same time with controlled pressure. Do not lock the brakes.

questions.question: If your front wheel locks while stopping, you should:

options.text: Release the front brake and use only the rear brake.
Release the front brake right away, then press it firmly again.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the front brake right away, then press it firmly again.
questions.explanation: If your front wheel locks, let go of the front brake immediately and then press it firmly again. Use both brakes when you need to stop quickly.

questions.question: When stopping, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes.
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes when slowing down or stopping. Using both brakes helps you stop quickly and safely.

questions.question: When approaching an intersection, a motorcyclist should NOT:

options.text: Choose a lane position that makes them more visible.
Speed up to cross the intersection quickly.
Get ready at the clutch and brakes to react faster.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up to cross the intersection quickly.
questions.explanation: As you approach an intersection, choose a lane position that other drivers can see. Get your hands ready at the clutch and brakes. Slow down when entering an intersection. Do not speed up or make sudden moves, as this may confuse other drivers.

questions.question: A motorcyclist is easiest to see when riding in which lane position?
questions.correctAnswerText: The center
questions.explanation: The center lane position is best when following a car because it puts you in the driver's rearview mirror where they can see you. Always be ready to change positions if traffic or road conditions change.

questions.question: _________ of collisions between motorcycles and cars are caused by drivers failing to give the right-of-way to the motorcyclist.
questions.correctAnswerText: More than half
questions.explanation: More than half of motorcycle and car collisions happen because drivers do not give the right-of-way to motorcyclists. Never assume that other drivers will yield to you, even if they should.

questions.question: The gearshift is located:
questions.correctAnswerText: By the left footrest.
questions.explanation: The gearshift lever is in front of the left footrest. You operate it with your left foot.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A stop sign is coming up ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A stop sign is coming up ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or pictures. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead. This sign warns you that a stop sign is coming.

questions.question: When making a normal stop on a motorcycle:

options.text: Use the front and rear brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the front and rear brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: For a normal stop, use the front and rear brakes together at the same time and downshift.

questions.question: When sitting on a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Use your arms to hold up your body.
Sit at an angle so your arms can support your weight.
Sit so you can use your arms to control the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sit so you can use your arms to control the motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Sit with good posture so you can use your arms to control the motorcycle. Your arms should not be used to hold up your body.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Railroad crossing ahead
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. They tell you about road conditions ahead. This sign warns you that a railroad crossing is coming.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: No right turn
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs are white with red and black markings. They tell you about traffic laws in that area. This sign means you cannot turn right.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Right lane ends
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. They tell you about road conditions ahead. This sign warns you that the right lane is ending.

questions.question: When attempting to pass another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Ride within the posted speed limits.
Exceed the posted speed limit to complete the pass, but not by more than 10 mph.
Pass more than one vehicle at a time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride within the posted speed limits.
questions.explanation: All passes must be done at legal speed limits. Only pass where it is safe and legal to do so.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Merge
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. They tell you about road conditions ahead. This sign warns you that traffic is merging ahead.

questions.question: You have an improved chance of avoiding serious injury in a crash if you wear:
questions.correctAnswerText: Face or eye protection.
questions.explanation: A helmet is your best protection in a crash. A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield helps protect your face from injury.

questions.question: If you borrow a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Assume all controls are in the same location as they are on your motorcycle.
Immediately take it out on the highway.
Get familiar with it in a controlled area.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get familiar with it in a controlled area.
questions.explanation: Every motorcycle is different. Before riding a new motorcycle, learn where all the controls are. Practice in a safe, controlled area before riding on the road.

questions.question: When riding, jackets and pants should:

options.text: Fit loosely enough to allow the wind to catch the fabric.
Be snug enough to keep from flapping in the wind.
Be tight enough to prevent you from moving freely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be snug enough to keep from flapping in the wind.
questions.explanation: Jackets and pants should fit snugly so they do not flap in the wind. They should also be loose enough that you can move freely.

questions.question: A flat front tire is especially dangerous because:

options.text: The front tire affects your steering, which also affects your balance.
The front tire being flat will disable the front brake.
The front tire being flat will prevent you from accelerating.

questions.correctAnswerText: The front tire affects your steering, which also affects your balance.
questions.explanation: A flat front tire is dangerous because it makes steering difficult. This affects your balance. Heavy steering may mean you have a flat front tire.

questions.question: You should flash your brake light to:

options.text: Tell other drivers that you are riding near them.
Help other drivers see your motorcycle in slow traffic.
Warn other drivers that you are slowing down or stopping unexpectedly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Warn other drivers that you are slowing down or stopping unexpectedly.
questions.explanation: Flash your brake light to warn drivers when you slow down or stop in places where they don't expect it. This is especially important before making tight, fast turns off high-speed roads.

questions.question: To improve your chances of being seen, you should:

options.text: Use your headlight only at night or in poor visibility.
Add an orange tint to your headlight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always use your headlight.
questions.explanation: Riding with your headlight on all the time is the best way to help other drivers see your motorcycle.

questions.question: If you must brake and swerve to avoid danger, you should:

options.text: Use only the front brake while swerving.
Brake and swerve at the same time.
Do one action first, then the other.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do one action first, then the other.
questions.explanation: Do braking and swerving as separate actions, not at the same time. Braking while swerving can cause your motorcycle to tip over.

questions.question: Riding on ______ may provide poor traction.
questions.correctAnswerText: Pavement markings
questions.explanation: Poor traction can happen on wet, snowy, icy, or muddy pavement; gravel roads; lane markings; and steel plates or utility hole covers.

questions.question: Taking a turn too fast can cause a rider to:

options.text: Drift into another lane of traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drift into another lane of traffic.
questions.explanation: Taking a turn too fast can cause you to drift into another lane or even leave the road. Always slow down before turning.
